entities.summary: Brigadier-General Ratu Epeli Nailatikau,, often referred to as Na Turaga Mai Naisogolaca, was a Fijian chief who was President of Fiji from 2009 to 2015. He had a long career in the Military, diplomatic service, and government. From 2001 to 2006 he served as Speaker of the House of Representatives – the lower and more powerful chamber of the Fijian Parliament. He was also the chairman of the Parliamentary Appropriations Committee and of the House Committee. On 8 January 2007, he was appointed the interim Minister for Foreign Affairs and External Trade; he was moved to the post of interim Minister for Provincial Development and Multi-Ethnic Affairs in September 2008.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As President of Fiji from 2009 to 2015, Epeli Nailatikau played a crucial role in stabilizing the country's government after a series of coups. His leadership helped maintain regional stability and paved the way for Fiji's transition to democracy.
